threshold_sources: Every v2 threshold comes only from (i) the spec, (ii) tech review section 7.2, (iii) the Phase 1 A controls and G2, or (iv) a per-state material-floor procedure declared here. No v2 threshold is derived from a cut_aware_surface_v1 (B v1) number.
rules: v1 verdicts (B v1 FAIL, Phase 3 gate FAIL) are kept and reported beside every v2 result forever.
This file is committed, with these reasons, before any v2-method measurement on physical states. v2 method development before the freeze may use only G2, zero-physics and affine controls.
Every v2 metric is applied identically to A, to B v1 and to B v2.

The full matrix {A, B v1, B v2} x {protocol v1, protocol v2} is reported on the saved states and on the held-out states, so metric relief (B v1 under v2 vs v1) is separated from method improvement (B v2 vs B v1 under the same protocol).

The saved phase3_surface_001 states were inspected while designing v2, so v2 is also decided on fresh held-out states declared below (new seeds; a new geometry per S-case where applicable; S8 with dense frames).
Smoothness and roughness are never success criteria (unchanged from v1).

P1_region_rule_v2.definition: A mesh vertex's mechanical component is taken from the extractor's own provenance, which both methods provide: CuttingSurface component_ranges (A) and CutAwareSurface component_ranges / vertex_component (B v1, B v2), mapped to the mass-ranked labels. Cut-face vs exterior, the cut row and the side then come from the nearest same-component boundary sample, exactly as region_rule_v1 (region_max 1.5 s; core = >= 3 s from the component's exterior samples). Every vertex gets a classification margin = (distance to the nearest sample of the next sample set) - (distance to the chosen set), the sets being {exterior, cut digit 0, cut digit 1, ...} of its component. MAX rows (current max, reference max) use only vertices with margin >= 0.5 s; P95/P50 rows and the bias/thickness means use all cut-face vertices; ambiguous vertices are counted and reported.
P1_region_rule_v2.justification: Inferring a vertex's component from its nearest particle is ill-posed whenever two pieces are closer than the drawing offset. The protocol itself places the material boundary at s/2 outside the particles (exterior samples x_p + F_p (s/2 e), surface_metrics_v1.exterior_samples), so any method that draws at that boundary has, between pieces less than 1 s apart, vertices nearer the other piece's particles; they are then measured against the opposite face's locus (review F1: 492 of 2,194 cut-face vertices in S6). Both extractors record the component of every vertex, so the metric need not guess. A nearest-sample classifier is undefined within s/2 of a rim or a junction of sets (review F6: every S5 vertex with reference error > 0.5 s is an exterior representative or a wrong-digit junction vertex); the rim is measured by the rim rows, so the max rows exclude only vertices whose class is not decided by at least s/2, while P95 rows keep every vertex. This holds for any method and does not use a B number.

P2_matched_scale_normal.definition: Decision normal row: for every core cut-face triangle (all three vertices core under P1; key = component, cut and side of its first vertex, as v1), the unsigned angle between the least-squares plane of the mesh's own cut-face vertices of the same key within 3 mm of the triangle centroid and the least-squares plane of the same-key locus side samples within 3 mm. Threshold per state: P95 over the core locus samples of the angle between the 3 mm planes fitted to two disjoint random halves of each side group's locus samples (numpy default_rng(20261031), groups in ascending key order), plus the 1 deg comparison band. S5 per-cut rows use the floor of that cut's samples. The v1 triangle-normal row (core triangles vs the 3 mm locus plane, 10 deg) stays reported, with its v1 value, as a shading/roughness diagnostic; it is not a v2 decision row.
P2_matched_scale_normal.justification: The reference is rough at about 0.3 s on 2 mm patches (the locus itself, review F4), and the protocol requires that physical roughness survive in current space and never be smoothed. A triangle-scale normal row compares a 1 mm facet with a 3 mm plane: a mesh built exactly through the locus samples scores 32-61 deg P95 against the 10 deg limit (review F4), so the v1 rows (distance rows that require following the locus, a normal row that only a smoothed mesh meets) are mutually unsatisfiable, contradicting smoothness_is_never_a_success_criterion and spec section 3.6. Comparing planes at the same 3 mm scale on both sides, against the locus's own split-half noise at that scale, measures orientation and not facet roughness. B-independent: the floor is a property of the state's locus only.

P3_current_distance_floor.definition: Current-space cut-face P95 row, per state and side group g = (component, cut, side): mesh P95_g (all P1 cut-face vertices of g) <= floor_g + 0.10 s, with floor_g = P95 over g's side samples of the leave-one-out residual |q_i - plane(other samples of g within 2 mm)| (min 4 neighbours, nearly collinear patches excluded as in local_plane_signed). Groups with < 20 cut-face vertices are pooled into one remainder group judged against the P95 of their samples' residuals. The row passes when every evaluated group passes; the pooled all-vertex P95 vs the pooled floor is reported. S5 per-cut rows use that cut's groups. Max limits unchanged: 1.5 s (S2 2.0 s), over P1-unambiguous vertices.
P3_current_distance_floor.offset_justification: 0.10 s = 2 x the tech review section 7.2 expectation for B with exact Hermite data (P95 <= 0.05 s); stated before any v2 measurement
P3_current_distance_floor.justification: The reference's own residual against its own 2 mm plane reaches P95 0.51 s with the sample inside the fit (review F4: G3b 0.512, S2 0.402, S6 0.437, S8 0.315), so a fixed 0.5 s P95 limit tests the material, not the mesh. A per-state floor from the locus alone (leave-one-out, so the sample is not in its own fit), plus a margin from the analytic expectation, keeps the row a test of the reconstruction. B-independent.

P4_current_volume_reference_precondition.definition: The 2 % current-volume row is kept. Before it decides, the reference sum (m/rho) det F is checked against the particle positions: fully linked cells = complete reference-lattice cells none of whose 12 edges is a conflicting link (any cut); per cell r = V(6 tetrahedra on the current positions) / (s^3 x mean corner det F); per mechanical component (>= 8 cells) CONSISTENT when |mean r - 1| <= 1 % and <= 5 % of its cells have r < 0.9, otherwise INCONSISTENT; components with < 8 cells are UNVERIFIED. The state's total row reads INCONCLUSIVE_REFERENCE (never PASS) when any verified component is INCONSISTENT or the UNVERIFIED components hold > 1 % of the reference volume (half the 2 % tolerance). The exact reference-volume rows (B: pre-embedding mesh vs sum m/rho) stay decisive and unchanged.
P4_current_volume_reference_precondition.justification: The current-volume reference contradicts the positions near the cut: the cell volumes from the particle positions fall to mean 0.77 (P5 0.15) within 1.5 mm of the Hermite locus while the solver's own F keeps det F ~ 0.999, and 87 % of the deficit lies within 3 mm (review F3, S5). A judge that contradicts the state cannot pass or fail a mesh that follows the state; it must report that the reference is inconsistent. The check uses only the state (positions, F, codes) and applies to every method.

P5_slow_motion_made_slow.definition: Slow-motion residual row on consecutive frame pairs without a code change whose material displacement P95 <= 0.10 s only (held-out S8 runs with dense snapshots, see held_out_states). Transport: each vertex of frame a moves by the inverse-distance-weighted (weights 1 / max(d, 1e-6 m)^2) displacement of its k = 8 nearest particles of its own provenance component at frame a. Residual = symmetric exact point-triangle distance between the transported mesh a and mesh b, P95, max over eligible pairs. Threshold 0.05 s unchanged. Topology-hash constancy over the frames stays the jump detector. With no eligible pair the row is NOT_RUN (premise unmet), never PASS.
P5_slow_motion_made_slow.justification: The v1 premise ('slow motion') was not met: the S8 snapshots are 40 ms apart and the material moves up to P95 0.46-0.48 s between them (review F10). Nearest-particle transport is a piecewise-constant displacement field whose own error grows with the strain increment, so it is not bounded below the 0.05 s threshold, which also lies below the protocol's declared 0.06 s uncertainty band. Making the frames slow and the transport interpolating restores the row's meaning (re-meshing jumps) without changing its threshold. Method-independent.

P6_intersection_attribution.definition: Intersecting triangle pairs (the v1 test and v1 sample bound: 20,000 triangles, seed 0) are split into PHYSICAL and UNEXPLAINED. Candidate physical: triangles of different mechanical components (provenance), or P1 cut-face triangles (>= 2 cut-face vertices) of opposite sides of the same cut digit in one component. A candidate is physical when, at the pair midpoint, the particle gap between the two sides' particle sets is < 1 s (min over both directions of the distance from the set's particle nearest the midpoint to the other set) or a locus row joining the two sides within 2 s has crossed sides ((q2 - q1) . N < 0). Every other pair, including every other intra-component (intra-shell) pair such as a fold, is unexplained. Likewise faces_nearer_other_component counts as unexplained only where the particle gap between the face's component and that other component near the face is >= 1 s. Only unexplained pairs and unexplained faces_nearer_other_component enter thresholds and the gate; physical pairs are reported as Phase 4 contact data.
P6_intersection_attribution.justification: The protocol places the material boundary at s/2 outside each piece (exterior samples x_p + F_p (s/2 e)), so represented volumes of pieces whose particles are closer than 1 s, or of slit sides that interpenetrate, physically overlap in the protocol's own convention (review F9). Drawing a physical overlap of represented volumes is fidelity, not a mesh defect; a method that shrinks pieces to avoid it hides the contact. Folds and any intersection without such proximity remain defects. Method-independent.

P7_S7_chip_accounting.definition: The S7 chip current-volume row (5 %) is evaluated on the lattice-faced part of the chip only: mesh volume of chip faces not produced by a particle-cell fallback vs sum (m/rho) det F of the chip particles not in that fallback, with the P4 precondition on the chip components (INCONCLUSIVE_REFERENCE when they are INCONSISTENT or UNVERIFIED). The particle-cell fallback part (M4 unlabelled_separation_v1) is reported separately as 'volume by construction', never as reconstruction quality and never in a cut-face metric. Methods without a fallback (A, B v1) have an empty fallback part. skipped_fragments = 0 unchanged.
P7_S7_chip_accounting.justification: A particle-cell fallback has the volume sum (m/rho) det F by construction, so counting it in the chip volume row would be a tautological PASS. Separating it keeps the row a test of the lattice-faced reconstruction and keeps any fallback visible. Method-independent (A and B v1 report an empty fallback part).

held_out_states.rule: Declared before any v2 measurement. Each S-case has H1 (v1 geometry, new placement seed) and H2 (new geometry inside the law-8 envelope where applicable, another new seed). For the drive_blade cases the 'seed' fixes the blade start offset inside the lattice cell: (u_x, u_y) = 0.15 + 0.7 * numpy.random.default_rng(seed).random(2), in spacings from the nearest lower cell face (cell faces at integer mm), replacing the v1 offsets (+0.3 / +0.2 mm). Values below are those offsets. Runner parameters otherwise as v1 (scripts/run_wp12_phase1_geometry.py PROTOCOL: 1 mm, 4 mm grid, 0.1 ms, law 8, tlmpm_v5, ruler_knife_v1, cutting energy 5 J/m^2, recorder on). Law-8 supported orientations (WP12_CUTTING_PHYSICS.md section 8, diagnostic, not a validated envelope): oblique through-cuts separate at theta <= 20 deg (known failure 25-45 deg), raked dome skims at rho 10-44 deg (known failure >= 45 deg). Every held-out cut below is vertical (theta = 0; yaw about z only) or a skim with rho inside 10-44 deg.
